comparison: Both strongly support the core trained immunity findings (C2, C30-C43). OpenEval emphasizes convergent evidence from multiple experimental approaches and dose-dependent responses. Peer reviewers describe results as 'solid' with 'rational approach' and 'interesting results,' affirming IS-induced trained immunity with augmented cytokine production.

Perfect agreement on uremic sera findings (C7, C45-C46, C91-C92). Both recognize this as providing translational relevance and clinical validation. OpenEval notes consistency between IS and uremic serum training. Peer reviewer highlights this as 'interesting and important' showing clinical relevance.

Complete agreement on metabolic reprogramming data (C47-C50). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of Seahorse data showing glycolytic and oxidative metabolism increases, noting 2-DG establishes glycolysis as necessary. Peer reviewers accept metabolic reprogramming as successfully demonstrated mechanism.

Strong agreement on epigenetic modifications (C51-C60). OpenEval provides comprehensive assessment of ChIP-qPCR and ChIP-seq evidence, noting MTA reversal supports causality. Peer reviewers explicitly accept 'epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming' as successfully demonstrated, with additional comments strengthening impact.

Both support AhR as critical mediator (C61-C68), though peer result R7 includes broader AhR claims (C3-C4, C69-C70). OpenEval emphasizes multiple complementary approaches and persistent nuclear AhR. Peer reviewers affirm 'AhR-mediated arachidonic acid pathway is required' as key claim, accepting AhR-dependent and -independent pathway distinction.

OpenEval addresses separability of AhR and metabolic pathways (C69-C70), noting dual mechanisms. Peer result R7 encompasses broader AhR mechanism including these claims along with C3-C4 and C61-C68, treating the AhR-dependent and -independent pathways as part of successfully demonstrated mechanism.

Strong agreement on transcriptomic evidence linking IS to AA metabolism via AhR (C71-C84). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of GSEA, pathway specificity, and convergent data. Peer reviewers specifically highlight 'AhR-mediated arachidonic acid pathway is required' as successfully demonstrated, accepting RNA-seq and ALOX5/ALOX5AP findings as key mechanistic advances.

Both support ALOX5/leukotriene pathway findings (C85-C90). OpenEval emphasizes multiple validation approaches and notes pathway acts downstream/parallel to mTOR. Peer reviewers accept these as part of AhR-arachidonic acid mechanism, treating pharmacological validation as strengthening mechanistic conclusions.

Agreement on epigenetic regulation mechanism (C93-C95). OpenEval notes lack of histone-modifying enzyme changes suggests regulation through other mechanisms. Peer reviewers accept these as part of mechanistic characterization supporting that metabolites rather than enzyme expression drive epigenetic changes.

Both support translational evidence in ESRD patients (C5-C6, C97-C102). OpenEval provides detailed analysis distinguishing acute from trained effects and notes adequate sample sizes. Peer reviewers treat this as 'interesting' evidence that 'IS plays a critical role' in CKD inflammatory responses, accepting as significant clinical validation.

Partial overlap on patient baseline data (C97-C98). OpenEval result R10 covers broader patient findings including trained responses and ALOX5 upregulation. Peer result R12 focuses specifically on baseline ex vivo responses, accepting these as part of clinical validation.

Agreement on in vivo mouse model validation (C8, C103-C106). OpenEval notes model recapitulates key features but acknowledges limitations regarding acute protocol and rapid IS clearance. Peer reviewers accept findings without critique, describing overall results as 'solid' and approach as 'rational.'

Complete agreement on peripheral vs. central trained immunity distinction (C107-C109). OpenEval notes negative BMDM results are important for understanding scope and consistent with acute training protocol. Peer reviewers accept characterization, treating it as clarifying scope and distinguishing peripheral from central immunity.

Perfect agreement on negative controls (C34-C36). OpenEval emphasizes these demonstrate specificity of IS effects and rule out trivial explanations. Peer reviewers accept without comment, describing overall approach as 'rational' and results as 'solid.'

Agreement on background claims establishing trained immunity concept (C1, C10-C19). OpenEval notes these are well-cited knowledge claims providing necessary context. Peer reviewers accept without question, affirming the work 'introduce[s] the important new concept of trained immunity' in CKD context.

Agreement on CKD and IS background (C20-C29). OpenEval notes these establish clinical relevance and prior knowledge. Peer result R14 encompasses broader background including these claims, accepting contextual framework without challenge.

Agreement on methodological context (C38, C44). OpenEval notes C38 establishes β-glucan as positive control and C44 justifies monocyte focus. Peer result R14 includes these among accepted background claims without question.

Agreement on IS concentration context (C32). OpenEval emphasizes this establishes physiological relevance of experimental concentrations. Peer result R14 includes this among accepted background claims.

Substantial overlap on discussion/interpretation claims (C110-C146). OpenEval notes interpretations are well-supported with appropriate acknowledgment of limitations. Peer result R14 accepts many of these background and contextual claims (C110, C112-C127, C129-C135, C137, C139-C143) without challenge.

Partial overlap on interpretive claims (C128, C136, C138, C144-C146). OpenEval treats these as appropriately tentative interpretations acknowledging limitations. Peer result R15 explicitly supports these as 'interesting' findings representing 'potential advance of the field,' particularly regarding IS role in CKD inflammatory responses.

Minor overlap on correlation analysis (C96). OpenEval result R9 includes this as validation of ChIP-seq and RNA-seq datasets. Peer result R6 encompasses broader epigenetic findings including this claim, accepting overall epigenetic data as strengthened.

Minimal overlap on ALOX5 patient data (C85). OpenEval result R8 includes this as part of functional validation. Peer result R8 focuses on broader transcriptomic evidence (C71-C85), accepting ALOX5 findings as part of successfully demonstrated AhR-AA pathway mechanism.
